CONFIRM C0001 — `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever a runner returns normally, but each runner returns `[]` on `_run_tool(...)->stderr=="NOT_FOUND"`. That makes missing binaries look available. The proposed fix direction is correct and blocks misleading endocrine health reports.

CONFIRM C0014 — `run_pyright()` copies `range.start.line` / `character` directly into `ToolDiagnostic`. Pyright JSON positions are 0-based; the rest of this module uses human-facing line numbers and mypy/bandit/ruff parsing yields 1-based rows. This creates off-by-one locations in health output and any downstream file/line attribution.

EXTEND C0021 | `evaluate_fix()` is also affected, not just `scan_health()`. Pre/post baselines use `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright|run_ruff|run_bandit, path)`, and those helpers currently treat timeout as zero findings because the runners parse empty output and return `[]`. Downstream consequence: a timed-out post-fix analysis can yield `net_* == 0`, causing `_compute_fix_verdict()` to classify the fix as `NEUTRAL` or `SAFE` instead of `UNEVALUABLE`/harmful. This crosses the interface into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4, which marks `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` fixes as `verified=True`, so a timeout can falsely close a bug.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox the codebase correctly for multi-file or import-dependent fixes. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it copies only the single target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit plus optional tests against that isolated file. The module advertises “sandbox-test proposed fixes” and “does the proposed fix break anything?”, but this implementation cannot detect breakage that depends on sibling modules, package-relative imports, or project config. Evidence from code: no package tree, config files, or sibling sources are copied; only one basename file is written into `tmpdir`, and test execution runs with `cwd=tmpdir`.
FOLLOW: Downstream, this can mark cross-file-breaking fixes as `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` because the sandbox lacks the imports and package context needed to expose the break. That directly feeds the immune pipeline’s Stage 4 in `immune_agents.py`, where `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` causes `verified=True`, enabling NK “bug closed” behavior in later rounds. In PoC terms this is HIGH: the system can silently certify a bad fix and suppress further review of the bug.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when evaluating a fix, copy the full relevant source tree into the temp directory (at minimum every file in `source_paths`, preserving relative paths), patch the target file in place inside that tree, and run analyzers/tests against the sandboxed tree rather than against a lone basename file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — optional test execution in `evaluate_fix()` can run against the wrong code, not the patched sandbox. The function writes the patched file into `tmpdir`, but then invokes the caller-supplied `test_cmd` unchanged with only `cwd=tmpdir`. If `test_cmd` contains absolute paths, repository-relative paths from project root, or module targets like `bench/tests/`, Python will import/read the real repo or simply fail to locate tests from inside `tmpdir`. There is no command rewriting, no copied test tree, and no environment isolation to force imports to come from the sandbox.
FOLLOW: The advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature can therefore produce false `tests_passed=True` against unmodified source or spurious failures unrelated to the fix. Either outcome contaminates `_compute_fix_verdict()`: bad fixes can be marked `SAFE`, or good fixes can be marked `HARMFUL`. This propagates into immune Stage 4 verification, affecting `verified=True` and later dedup/closure decisions across rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — before running tests, copy the referenced test files/directories needed by `test_cmd` into the sandbox alongside the source tree and rewrite path arguments in `test_cmd` to point at the sandboxed locations so tests necessarily execute against patched code.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses aggregated net issue count (`total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`) and treats only `total_net > 0` as harmful. This allows regressions in one tool to be canceled by improvements in another. Example from the code’s logic: a fix that introduces 3 new bandit findings but removes 4 ruff warnings yields `total_net = -1` and is classified `SAFE`. That violates the module’s stated purpose of deciding whether a proposed fix is SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL.
FOLLOW: Downstream consequence is silently wrong fix certification: a security or type regression can be masked by unrelated lint reduction. Because immune Stage 4 marks `SAFE` and `NEUTRAL` fixes as verified, the system can programmatically bless a harmful fix and then close out later duplicate findings via the NK bug-closed gate.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify a fix as `HARMFUL` if any individual net metric is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); only treat it as `SAFE` when no metric regresses and at least one improves or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` matches paths by substring (`if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`) over `finding.description + " " + finding.proposed_fix`. This can select the wrong file when one path name is a substring of another, or when a basename appears in descriptive prose. Example class of failure from the implementation: a mention of `brain.py` can match any source path containing that substring, not necessarily the cited file. The function then falls back to `source_paths[0]`, making mis-targeting silent.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` may patch and analyze the wrong file while reporting the original finding ID. That makes fix evaluation results meaningless and can falsely label a fix `UNEVALUABLE`, `SAFE`, or `HARMFUL` for unrelated code. Because these verdicts feed immune verification and later bug closure, wrong-file targeting can silently corrupt the system’s review state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict matching to normalized path equality on basename or suffix path segments only; if multiple candidates match or none match, return `None` and mark the evaluation `UNEVALUABLE` instead of guessing `source_paths[0]`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the health-scan interface claims static analysis runs `pyright/ruff/bandit` and the header advertises `mypy` and `crosshair` binaries, but fix evaluation baselines and post-fix checks only count pyright, ruff, and bandit. `run_mypy()` exists but is never used in `evaluate_fix()`, and crosshair is declared but completely unused. For fix safety, type regressions detectable only by mypy never influence the SAFE/HARMFUL verdict.
FOLLOW: A proposed fix can worsen mypy-only type errors and still be marked `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL`. That undermines the “whole-body health monitor” contract and can allow bad fixes to become `verified=True` in immune Stage 4. Cross-tool inconsistency also makes endocrine health and endocrine fix evaluation disagree about what “type health” means.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — include mypy in pre/post fix counts and verdict computation, using the existing `run_mypy()` runner; leave crosshair out of PoC behavior entirely unless it is actually wired in.
VERIFIED: TRUE

CONFIRM C0015 — response-size anomaly currently emits `signal_type="context_growth"` in check 4, which aliases a distinct condition into the wrong channel. The fix to use a distinct signal type is correct.

CONFIRM C0008 — both slow-model and response-size anomaly use upper-middle element selection instead of a true median. For even counts, this inflates the baseline and can suppress signals. `statistics.median()` is the right minimal correction.
